page.overview:
Who is Alexis Fairburn?

Alexis Fairburn, born Alexei Fyodorov, was a schoolmaster employed as a professor of mathematics at Eton College, in Berkshire, England. The character was first introduced in the author Charlie Higson's 2007 Young Bond novel Double or Die.

Fairburn was born Alexei Fyodorov, to a Russian mother and English father, and grew up in England where he took the name Alexis Fairburn. After the First World War he studied mathematics at Cambridge University; where he met fellow students, Ivar Peterson (mathematics) and John Charnage (chemistry). He went on to teach the subject at Eton College, moonlighting as a crossword writer for The Times and was chair of Eton's Crossword Society. In 1933, Fairburn (alongside Peterson) was hired by Charnage to construct a complex calculating machine dubbed "N.E.M.E.S.I.S". He left when he deduced the true nature of their project: a code-breaking machine for the Soviet Union. Fearful of Russian reprisals, Charnage hired contract-killers Wolfgang and Ludwig Smith to kidnap Fairburn and forced him to resume construction.

On 7th December 1933, Fairburn wrote a cryptic SOS letter to his star student, Pritpal Nandra; hoping he would take it to the police. Initially believing it to be an eccentric game, the boys unravelled the clues hidden in the letter. On 17th December, James Bond and his friends discovered that Fairburn and his mechanical creation were being held aboard a cargo ship in London. Arriving just before its scheduled departure for the Soviet Union, James and Kelly Kelly snatched Fairburn from under Charnage's nose and hid overnight aboard a nearby luxury liner. The next morning Soviet operatives boarded the vessel. They fought their way out; but the wharf below was swarming with Charnage's men. As they prepared to surrender an army of dock workers loyal to the Kelly family arrived to fight them off. Perry Mandeville attempted to escort Fairburn to safety, but they were taken captive by Colonel Irina Sedova. Bond searched the abandoned pneumatic rail tunnels - eventually finding them in an old engine room for the fans that ran the railway. Fairburn was knocked unconscious during the standoff; only regaining consciousness after Sedova had fled.

Thirteen years later, at the close of the Second World War, Commander Bond was sent to Bletchley Park to bring Fairburn back to London for debriefing at the ministry headquarters. Fairburn had been working at "Site X", where his mathematics skills had been put to use as a code-breaker alongside Alan Turing. Turing's calculating machines proved far more powerful than his N.E.M.E.S.I.S. machine had been; leading him to muse that Colonel Sedova had kidnapped the wrong man. He and Bond then discussed the future of warfare: Fairburn's stance on which, was that wars would increasingly be fought by intellectuals and machines.
